title: ORDER BY on a column holding numbers and text puts the numbers first
query: EVALUATE SELECTCOLUMNS ( T, "v", IF ( T[n] = 2, "x", T[n] ) ) ORDER BY [v]

source.quote: DAX considers Boolean values greater than string values, and string values greater than numeric or date/time values
source.supports: the rank of types in comparisons: numbers and dates lowest, then strings, then booleans

source.quote: The Variant data type is used for expressions that might return different data types, depending on the conditions
source.supports: an IF with an integer branch and a string branch is a variant expression

derivation: T[n] holds 1, 2, 3. The expression gives 1, "x", 3: a variant column. String values rank above numeric values, so ascending order is the numbers in order and then the text: 1, 3, "x".
alternative: The ranking rule is documented for comparison expressions, not for ORDER BY. If ORDER BY does not accept a variant column the query fails with an error; if text sorted before numbers the order would be "x", 1, 3.
